newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil stocks end firm on local buy orders.
newsitem.headline: Brazil stocks end firm on local buy orders.

text.p: After falling for three consecutive sessions, Brazilian shares jumped 3.46 percent at the close in heavy trade on buy orders from domestic mutual funds and banks, brokers said.
The Bovespa index .BVSP of the 48 most active stocks rose 434 points, closing at 13,002 points. Market turnover returned to its recent high levels, totalling 1.04 billion reais ($971 million).
"The buying spree was led by local stock funds and banks for their own portfolios," said a senior trader.
Analysts think funds decided to rebuild positions after the last declines.
"Many funds sold in the last days of the first half. But now it's a new semester. Fresh money is coming in and they (the funds) are allocating the cash," another trader said.

Recently, stock funds have seen net inflows of nearly 100 million reais a day on average. Equity funds currently account for 10 percent of the Brazilian fund industry, up from 3.0-4.0 percent in December last year.
One factor that helped bolster the market was the general expectation that the U.S. Federal Reserve will leave U.S. interest rates unchanged.
The Fed began meeting Tuesday and is expected to announce a decision on rates Wednesday. Traders noted the bolsa had lost ground midafternoon but rebounded late in the session, led by blue-chips.
Bellwether Telebras preferred surged 4.53 percent to 170.70 reais.
Federal power holding Eletrobras preferred closed up 3.27 percent at 663 reais, while its voting stock rose 2.99 percent to close at 620 reais.
Oil state firm Petrobras preferred ended up 1.67 percent at 304 reais.
Private miner Vale do Rio Doce rose 1.22 percent to 24.10 reais.
Government bank Banco do Brasil continued climbing, surging 7.6 percent to end at 13.88 reais on market speculation of higher earnings.

Despite the continued inflow of cash, some analysts are now more cautious about the bolsa after its spectacular rise so far this year. They are recommending investors build positions in liquid stocks as volatility is likely to increase.

"The outlook for the Brazilian bolsa, based on the scenario of economic stability in the next years, is very favorable, but in the short-term it is important to be aware of the market's accumulated rise, which may increase volatility," said Lloyds Bank Brazil in this week's report.
